trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.location: Generalitat de Catalunya, 6, Sant Just Desvern, ES (41.3772,2.0791)

experiences.description: Explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica with a skip-the-line guided tour. Marvel at the intricate facades, stunning stained glass windows, and learn about the century-long construction history. Climb the towers for panoramic city views.

experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Barcelona's legendary public market on La Rambla. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, seafood, and fresh-squeezed juices from the vibrant stalls. A true feast for the senses and a cultural institution since 1217.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to L1 toward Sant Just Desvern area, or take a budget bus (Aerobús ~€6.75) to Plaça Catalunya and connect onward. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short evening stroll around Sant Just Desvern's local streets to get oriented and grab a light bite at a nearby neighbourhood bar.

meals.dinner: Bar or neighbourhood tavern near the hotel – look for a 'menú del día' or bocadillo (sandwich) for €5–8. Try Bar Restaurant Can Rafel or any local tapas bar in Sant Just Desvern.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – you land late. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport or first metro station; it covers all metro/bus rides and will save money across the trip. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance since arrival is after 19:00.

day_by_day.morning: Head into central Barcelona via metro (L1 from Hospitalet/Torrassa area). Visit the Gothic Quarter on a self-guided or budget walking tour. Explore the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30), Roman ruins of Barcino, Plaça Sant Jaume, and the narrow medieval lanes. Pick up a free map at the tourist office near Plaça Catalunya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes from the Gothic Quarter to La Boqueria Market on La Rambla. Enjoy the La Boqueria Market Food Experience – sample fresh fruit, jamón ibérico, olives, and cheap tapas from market stalls (budget €8–12 for a self-curated tasting lunch). Afterwards, stroll La Rambla and explore El Raval neighbourhood. Visit the free courtyard of the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) for architecture interest.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's famous nightlife on a budget. Head to the El Raval or Barceloneta area for pre-drinks at a cheap bar (cañas of beer from €1.50–2.50). Many clubs don't fill up until midnight – look for free-entry flyers distributed near La Rambla for clubs like Sala Apolo or Moog. Enjoy the buzzing street atmosphere of Carrer Blai (Poble Sec) for cheap pintxos.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant or tostada at a local café near the hotel or near Plaça Catalunya – budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: La Boqueria Market stalls – fresh fruit, croquetas, jamón, and a drink for €8–12.
meals.dinner: Carrer Blai in Poble Sec – pintxos bars where each bite-sized snack costs €1–1.50. Fill up for €8–10 with a drink included.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks around 28–29°C – carry a reusable water bottle (public fountains are free across the city). La Boqueria is busiest midday; arrive by 13:00 to avoid the worst crowds. Gothic Quarter walking is entirely free.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Sagrada Família Guided Tour in advance online (skip-the-line tickets ~€26–33 with tower access). Take the metro L2/L5 to Sagrada Família station. Arrive at opening (09:00) to beat the heat and crowds. The guided tour covers Gaudí's visionary architecture, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the breathtaking interior forest of columns and stained glass. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short metro ride to Gràcia neighbourhood. Explore Gaudí's Casa Vicens (exterior free, interior ~€16 – skip interior to save budget) and stroll the charming Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Walk uphill toward Park Güell – enter the free monumental zone perimeter for exterior views, or book the paid Monumental Zone ticket (~€10) in advance if budget allows. The park offers stunning panoramic views of Barcelona.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample district for the famous 'Manzana de la Discordia' – walk past Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera on Passeig de Gràcia (all free to admire from outside). As night falls, head to Eixample's Gayxample area or Carrer del Consell de Cent for lively, affordable bars. Many bars offer free entry and cheap drinks during happy hour (19:00–21:00).

meals.breakfast: Granja or traditional café near Sagrada Família – pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and coffee for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a restaurant in Gràcia neighbourhood – 3 courses with bread and drink for €11–13. Look for chalkboard signs outside local restaurants.
meals.dinner: Eixample tapas bar – patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and a glass of house wine. Budget €10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead for August – they sell out fast. Park Güell's free zones are accessible anytime but the paid Monumental Zone requires timed entry tickets. Wear comfortable shoes – lots of walking and hills today.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta beach for a morning swim and walk along the seafront promenade (Passeig Marítim). The beach is free and beautiful in the morning before it gets too crowded. Walk north along the waterfront to the Port Olímpic area and admire Frank Gehry's iconic golden 'Fish' sculpture – a great architecture photo stop. Explore the Poblenou neighbourhood, Barcelona's creative tech district with interesting street art and converted industrial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Parc de la Ciutadella – Barcelona's green lung. See the monumental cascade fountain (partly designed by a young Gaudí), the lake, and the Catalan Parliament building exterior. Walk through the Ribera neighbourhood to the Santa Maria del Mar church (free entry, stunning Gothic architecture) and the El Born cultural district. Browse the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colourful alternative to La Boqueria, less touristy) for an afternoon snack.
day_by_day.evening: El Born and La Ribera come alive at night. Start with vermouth (vermut) at a traditional bar around 19:00 – a classic Barcelona ritual costing €2–3. Then explore the nightlife scene: Bar del Pla, El Xampanyet (famous cava bar), or head to the waterfront clubs near Port Olímpic. Many beach clubs have free entry before midnight. Enjoy the warm August night by the sea.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh juice and pastry from a bakery near Barceloneta – €3–4.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina or a bocadillo from a local bar in El Born – €5–7.
meals.dinner: El Born neighbourhood – look for set dinner menus or share tapas at a local bar. Budget €10–13. Try El Xampanyet for cava and anchovies (a Barcelona classic).

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta beach gets very crowded by 11:00 in August – go early. Watch your belongings on the beach and in crowded areas. The Parc de la Ciutadella is free and a great midday escape from the heat. Santa Maria del Mar church is architecturally stunning and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or FGC train to Montjuïc. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (€12.70 return) or hike up for free via the gardens path. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró exterior and the free Jardins de Laribal. Explore the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry or free on first Sunday of month) for panoramic views over Barcelona, the port, and the sea. The hilltop architecture and fortifications are impressive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Poble Sec and visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe – the reconstructed 1929 Barcelona Pavilion, a landmark of modernist architecture (€7 entry, well worth it for architecture lovers). Walk through Montjuïc's free Olympic Ring area – see the 1992 Olympic Stadium exterior and the futuristic Palau Sant Jordi by Arata Isozaki. End the afternoon with a final wander through the Eixample to photograph any Modernista buildings you missed.
day_by_day.evening: Final night in Barcelona – make it memorable on a budget. Head to Tibidabo area or back to El Raval/Gothic Quarter for a farewell dinner. Splurge slightly on a nicer menú del día dinner (€15–18). Afterwards, enjoy one last night out: rooftop bars in Eixample offer sunset views (many free entry with a drink purchase ~€6–8). End the night dancing at a club – look for free-entry promotions online via apps like Xceed or Fever.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a café con leche and tostada near the hotel – €3–4.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc – buy supplies from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) for €5–7: bread, cheese, fruit, and a cold drink.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Gothic Quarter or El Raval – slightly elevated budget of €15–18 for a proper sit-down menú del día or shared tapas spread with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details and plan transport back to the airport accordingly (allow 60–90 minutes from Sant Just Desvern). The Pavelló Mies van der Rohe is a must for architecture enthusiasts – one of the most influential buildings of the 20th century. Keep €10–15 aside for any last-minute transport or airport costs.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 19:20. Use morning for in-flight rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Still in transit. Arrive Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20, clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern (~25 min by taxi or Aerobus + local taxi, approx €30–40). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Casual first-night dinner near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern. Stroll the quiet local streets to decompress from travel. Explore the immediate neighbourhood, grab a drink at a nearby bar, and get an early night to prepare for a full Day 2.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick bite at Barcelona El Prat Airport (try a bocadillo at one of the terminal cafés, ~€6–8).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Can Ramonet or a local neighbourhood restaurant near Sant Just Desvern – look for a menú del día or tapas spread. Budget ~€20–28 per person. Try patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and a glass of house Catalan wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance as arrival is after 19:00. Download the TMB Barcelona Metro app and purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro card the next morning. Weather in August averages 28.9°C – stay hydrated on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour (pre-booked skip-the-line tickets essential – book online before the trip). Take the metro from Sant Just Desvern area into central Barcelona (L3 or bus connection). Arrive at the basilica by 9:00–9:30 AM before the heat peaks. Spend 2–2.5 hours marvelling at Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece – the Nativity façade, Passion façade, and the soaring interior forest of columns. The guided tour provides rich architectural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short taxi to the Eixample district. Explore the Modernista architecture along Passeig de Gràcia – admire the exterior of Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Casa Amatller on the 'Block of Discord'. If budget allows, enter La Pedrera (~€25) for rooftop views. Spend the afternoon soaking in Gaudí's urban vision at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the El Born / Sant Pere neighbourhood for dinner and a first taste of Barcelona's nightlife. Wander the narrow medieval streets, pop into a cocktail bar, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere as the city comes alive after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café – café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a croissant or tostada amb tomàquet (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca in Eixample – excellent mid-range tapas and montaditos. Budget ~€18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born – a beloved traditional cava bar serving tapas and house cava. Arrive early (19:30–20:00) as it fills up fast. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance for August. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a water bottle. The Eixample grid is very walkable. August evenings stay warm (~22–24°C) – perfect for outdoor dining.

day_by_day.morning: La Boqueria Market Food Experience. Take the metro to Liceu (L3) and arrive at La Boqueria on La Rambla by 9:00 AM before the tourist crowds surge. Immerse yourself in the legendary market – sample fresh fruit, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, and seafood pintxos at the market bars. This is a sensory feast and a genuine Barcelona cultural institution. Budget ~€15–20 for tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour. After the market, step directly into the adjacent Gothic Quarter for a guided or self-guided walking tour. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the old Jewish Quarter (El Call), and hidden medieval courtyards. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the labyrinthine streets. Rest in the shade of Plaça de Sant Felip Neri during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit. Take a short walk or taxi to Barceloneta Beach for a golden-hour sunset stroll along the Mediterranean (sunset ~20:45 in August). Then transition into El Born for the nightlife circuit – start with craft cocktails at a rooftop bar, move to a tapas dinner, and finish the night dancing at one of El Born's stylish clubs or live music venues.

meals.breakfast: Eat at La Boqueria itself – fresh-squeezed orange juice, a slice of tortilla española, and seasonal fruit from the market stalls (~€8–12).
meals.lunch: Bar Cañete near the Gothic Quarter – excellent traditional Catalan cuisine with a lively atmosphere. Try the croquetas and grilled fish. Budget ~€22–30 per person.
meals.dinner: El Born district – dinner at Bar del Pla (Catalan tapas, great value) followed by cocktails at Paradiso (ranked among the world's best bars, hidden behind a pastrami shop). Budget ~€25–35 per person for dinner + drinks.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is best visited early – by 11:00 AM it becomes very crowded. Keep valuables secure on La Rambla (pickpocket hotspot). Barceloneta Beach can be busy in August; bring sunscreen if you plan to linger. Barcelona nightlife starts late – clubs typically fill up after midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood Exploration. Book timed-entry tickets to the Monumental Zone of Park Güell in advance (~€10). Take the metro to Lesseps or Vallcarca and walk up (or take the free escalators from Carrer de Lesseps). Arrive at 9:00 AM for the best light and fewer crowds. Explore the iconic mosaic terraces, the gingerbread gatehouses, the hypostyle room, and enjoy sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona and the Mediterranean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Park Güell into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood below. This bohemian, village-like barrio is full of independent boutiques, art galleries, and leafy plazas. Wander Carrer de Verdi, browse local shops, and relax in Plaça del Sol or Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. In late afternoon, consider visiting the Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work, ~€16) nearby for more architectural depth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample or El Born area for a more relaxed evening. Visit a rooftop bar for sunset cocktails (try the terrace at Hotel Pulitzer or Azimuth Rooftop), then enjoy a leisurely dinner. This is a good night for a slightly more indulgent mid-range restaurant experience as a trip highlight.

meals.breakfast: Café in the Gràcia neighbourhood before heading up to Park Güell – try Federal Café on Carrer del Parlament (a short detour) or a local bakery near the metro. Budget ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Gràcia – La Pepita (creative bocadillos and tapas) or Parking Pizza (excellent Neapolitan-style pizza in a fun setting). Budget ~€15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample – a beloved neighbourhood wine bar and restaurant with excellent Catalan dishes and an impressive wine list. Budget ~€28–38 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed-entry tickets sell out weeks in advance in August – book before your trip. Wear sturdy shoes as the paths are uneven. The walk up to the park is steep; the escalator route from Lesseps is easier. Gràcia is quieter and more local-feeling than the tourist centre – a great contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning. Sleep in slightly after the nightlife-heavy itinerary. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast, then take a final walk along Barceloneta Beach or the Port Olímpic waterfront. Browse the Barceloneta neighbourhood's local market (Mercat de la Barceloneta) for last-minute food souvenirs – local olive oil, saffron, or Catalan wines. Take a final dip in the Mediterranean if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration based on any missed highlights. Options: revisit a favourite neighbourhood, visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art, ~€12) near the Raval for an air-conditioned cultural experience, or browse the antique and vintage shops along Carrer de la Palla in the Gothic Quarter. Begin packing and preparing for departure. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Barcelona before heading back to the hotel or airport. Choose a restaurant that captures the essence of the trip – great Catalan food, good wine, and the warm August evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighbourhood café – try churros con chocolate at a traditional granja, or a full tostada spread. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside chiringuito (beach bar) on Barceloneta – grilled sardines, gambas al ajillo, and a cold Estrella Damm beer. Budget ~€18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Tickets (Albert Adrià's tapas bar – book well in advance) for a splurge, or the more accessible Bodega 1900 nearby for elevated vermouth-bar cuisine. Alternatively, a classic paella at La Mar Salada near Barceloneta. Budget ~€30–45 per person for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 12:00 noon) and arrange luggage storage if your departure is later in the day. Keep a transit budget for the return journey to the airport. August 47.5mm monthly rainfall means occasional afternoon thunderstorms are possible – carry a light rain layer. Tip: buy a bottle of Catalan cava at a local shop as a take-home souvenir (~€8–15 for an excellent bottle).

meals.lunch: Lunch at Alkimia or Bodega Sepúlveda in the Eixample district — refined Catalan cuisine with a modern twist in a sophisticated setting

Discover Roman ruins beneath the city streets, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards that most tourists miss. A private guide will bring 2,000 years of history to life through storytelling and exclusive access points.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience: Head to La Rambla for an immersive premium food experience at the legendary Mercat de la Boqueria. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, artisan cheeses, exotic fruits, and local delicacies with a curated food guide. Follow with a visit to the nearby Palau de la Música Catalana — a UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall — for a guided interior tour of its stunning stained-glass ceiling and ornate facade.

Dine at a Michelin-starred restaurant, then head to Opium Barcelona or Pacha Barcelona for a premium nightclub experience along the waterfront.

meals.dinner: Dinner at Disfrutar — a three-Michelin-star restaurant offering one of the world's most innovative tasting menus, a true bucket-list dining experience in Barcelona

day_by_day.notes: Disfrutar and Tickets require reservations made months in advance — confirm before the trip. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot in the morning before the heat peaks. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Architecture Deep Dive — Eixample Modernisme Route: Spend the morning on a self-guided or private-guided tour of Barcelona's Eixample district, the heart of Catalan Modernisme. Visit Casa Batlló (book the premium 'Magic Nights' experience or the standard morning tour with AR glasses) and Casa Milà (La Pedrera), two of Gaudí's most celebrated residential masterpieces. Explore the rooftop of La Pedrera for iconic views of the city's skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc & Poble Sec Exploration: Take a private car or cable car up to Montjuïc for sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art, and stroll through the Jardins de Laribal. Descend into the Poble Sec neighborhood for a relaxed afternoon exploring its emerging food and arts scene — visit the Refugi 307 underground Civil War shelter for a fascinating historical detour.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at La Isabela rooftop bar at the Hotel 1898 on La Rambla, followed by a premium dinner in the Eixample. Cap the night with a visit to a sophisticated jazz bar — Jamboree Jazz Club in Plaça Reial hosts world-class live performances nightly — for a more refined nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Forn de Sant Jaume on Passeig de Gràcia — an iconic Eixample bakery and café with exquisite pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bodega 1900 (another Albert Adrià concept) in Poble Sec — a premium vermouth bar and restaurant reimagining classic Spanish tavern food with haute cuisine techniques
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lasarte — a three-Michelin-star restaurant by Martín Berasategui in the Eixample, offering an extraordinary Basque-Catalan tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book Casa Batlló and La Pedrera tickets online in advance. The 'Magic Nights' experience at Casa Batlló (evenings) is a spectacular alternative if preferred. August evenings are warm and perfect for rooftop dining.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Morning & Luxury Shopping: Start the final day slowly with a premium breakfast and a relaxed morning stroll along Passeig de Gràcia — Barcelona's most elegant boulevard. Browse luxury boutiques including Loewe, Hermès, and local Catalan designers. Visit the Bloc de la Discòrdia to admire the three competing modernista masterpieces side by side: Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poblenou & 22@ Innovation District Architecture Walk: Explore Barcelona's cutting-edge contemporary architecture in the Poblenou district — the city's reinvented industrial quarter now home to striking modern buildings, street art, and design studios. Visit the Rambla del Poblenou for a local, unhurried atmosphere. End with a final visit to the waterfront at Port Olímpic for a last look at the Mediterranean.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Final Night: Enjoy a spectacular farewell dinner at a premium waterfront restaurant. Afterward, take a final evening walk along La Rambla and through the Gothic Quarter to soak in Barcelona's magical nighttime atmosphere. Return to the hotel for a comfortable final night before departure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Mauri Pastisseria on Passeig de Gràcia — a legendary Barcelona patisserie open since 1929, perfect for croissants, cakes, and café amb llet
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rías de Galicia in the Eixample — one of Barcelona's finest seafood restaurants, celebrated for its Galician shellfish and premium wine list
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Enoteca Paco Pérez at Hotel Arts Barcelona — a two-Michelin-star restaurant with stunning port views, offering an exceptional Mediterranean tasting menu to close the trip in style

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. Pre-book the farewell dinner reservation. Consider a private transfer back to the airport for a seamless luxury conclusion to the trip.
